sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Direct Online Retail of Portable Battery Generators and Solar Panels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system) with hybrid elements under Private Interest Foundation statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, in force 2012)
Panama–South Korea Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 2015 (amended by Law 70 of 2019) on Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism; Executive Decree 559 of 2013; Law 52 of 2016 (Beneficial Ownership of Legal Entities); Regulation No. JS-08-2018 of the Public Registry; Resolution No. UAF-DG-01-2020 of the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF); Cabinet Decree No. 3 of 2013 (AML/CFT supervisory framework); and the 'Single Text of Law 47 of 2013' as amended by Law 23 of 2015.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Panama is a Hague Apostille member) or Consular Legalization if origin is non-Hague jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of Panama / Registered Agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the Notarized Foundation Council Resolution appointing officers and protectors
Certificate of Registered Agent and Registered Office
Beneficial Ownership Registry submission receipt (UBO Register under Law 52 of 2016)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized proof of identification and address of founders, council members, protector, and ultimate beneficial owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Notary or competent authority in the jurisdiction of each individual

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory rolling screening of all Directors, Foundation Council members, Protectors, Beneficial Owners, and authorized signatories against international sanctions listings (OFAC SDN, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, UK HMT) and PEP databases. Panama Law 23 of 2015 and UAF Resolutions require risk-based enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons and ongoing transaction monitoring. The online retail scope ('solar portable power') requires validation that counterparties do not involve any sanctioned jurisdiction or designated entities. Automated screening must be performed pre-incorporation and repeated at every significant transaction threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) online name reservation system via registered agents; official portal: 'Servicio en Línea de Nombre Reservado' at www.registropublico.gob.pa
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All foundation names must be submitted in Latin characters; if the intended name uses non-Latin script, a transliteration or Spanish adaptation must be filed. The name must contain the words 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or the abbreviation 'P.I.F.' or 'Foundation' where applicable, per Law 25 of 1995. The name may not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered entity, and must observe public order, good customs, and the jurisdiction's prohibition on misleading terms.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name reservation is rejected, the registered agent may submit an appeal to the Public Registry's Departamental Oficialía Mayor requesting reconsideration within 5 business days of notification, attaching a printed reservation ticket and explanation of validity. If the name is denied due to prohibited terms or similarity, a new alternative name may be immediately reserved for a further 30-day window. A formal administrative appeal may then be filed under the Procedural Unity Law (Law 38 of 2001) before the Public Registry's Superior Authority or in the First Circuit Administrative Litigation Court.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only if backed by a licensed Panamanian registered agent with a physical address in Panama. The foundation business model (online solar retail) may operate remotely without local employees, but the statutory registered office must be maintained by the registered agent. The Public Registry does not require a separate local operational storefront for an e-commerce entity; however, commercial substance expectations under Law 254 of 2021 (Economic Substance Act) require that core income-generating activities be adequately managed from or through the registered agent's location if banking or tax domicile in Panama is claimed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for online retail: estimated 15-25% chance of unannounced on-site inspection within the first two years to verify registered office signage and agent availability; higher if the entity is selected for economic substance audit or AML inspection by the Financial Analysis Unit.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 26 de mayo de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Ley No. 32 de 26 de febrero de 2011; particularly Articles 1-26, including endowment, registered office, resident agent, and council provisions, together with the applicable regulations of the Registro Público de Panamá.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá), Private Interest Foundation Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública de Constitución de Fundación de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No paid-up share capital applies to a Private Interest Foundation. The foundation must maintain an initial endowment sufficient to achieve its purposes; standard Panamanian foundation practice requires an endowment of at least USD 10,000. The endowment is contributed in cash or assets and is not deposited in an escrow account; it forms autonomous patrimony managed by the Foundation Council.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The Founder and initial Foundation Council of Private Interest Foundation PA_PIF accept the endowment of ten thousand United States Dollars (USD 10,000) contributed as the foundation's patrimony, to be maintained separately for the accomplishment of its online solar power retail purpose under ISIC 4791. The registered office is fixed at the law office of the Resident Agent in Panama City, Republic of Panama. The Resident Agent is appointed for statutory representation and regulatory service. The Foundation Council is constituted with [Name] as President and [Name] as Secretary, each holding office until resignation, incapacity, or removal by the Founder. All council members accept the duties under Law 25 of 1995.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and notarial execution of the foundation charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público (Notary Public) of the First Judicial Circuit of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founder and the resident agent prepare the Spanish-language foundation charter. The founder appears before a Panamanian notary, declares the initial endowment of USD 10,000, and signs the charter together with the resident agent and the designated Foundation Council members. The notary authenticates the instrument and issues the protocol index and first transcript for registration.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or identity card of the founder
Proof of the registered office address in Panama
Acceptance letter from the proposed Resident Agent
Acceptance letter from each Foundation Council member
Draft Foundation Charter (Escritura Pública) in Spanish
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses execution, correct the identified defect or engage another notary; a fresh signing and protocolization is required for any altered clause.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of registry insertion and stamp fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry Treasury Office and online payment platform of the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, pay the official registry fee and applicable stamp taxes using the Registry's online payment portal or in-person cashier. Obtain the official payment receipt showing the exact folio and foundation name, then attach it to the registration filing.
required_dossiers: Notarial protocol index and first transcript
Foundation identification details for payment reference
Registry fee payment form (solicitud de pago)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment is rejected or assigned a wrong folio, obtain a corrected payment slip from the Registry, apply the payment to the correct file number, and resubmit without delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the foundation with the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá - Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original notarized charter, the first transcript, and the fee receipt with the Private Interest Foundation Section. The Registry examiner verifies the foundation name, lawful purpose, endowment, registered office, resident agent, and council appointments, then records the foundation and issues an electronic certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Original Escritura Pública de Constitución
First transcript of the notarial protocol
Official fee and stamp tax payment receipt
Completed registry application form (solicitud de inscripción)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect observation (reparos), file a written clarification and, if required, a correction deed within ten business days; for substantive defects, submit an amendment for separate registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer registration with the national revenue authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the registered foundation charter and resident agent documentation, file the RUC/NIT registration application with the DGI. Provide the purpose of the online retail business and indicate that the foundation is subject to territorial income tax and, if applicable, will collect 7% ITBMS on taxable online sales. Receive the RUC certificate and tax status letter.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration from the Public Registry
Registered Foundation Charter
Identity card or passport of the Resident Agent
Proof of address of the registered office
RUC/NIT application form obtained from the DGI
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the application due to inconsistencies, correct the data, pay any late-registration fine, and resubmit via the same electronic form; submit an administrative reconsideration if the rejection persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal commercial operation notice for online retail and warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) - Economic Viability Directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación de Establecimiento Comercial for the online retail activity and, if a storage location exists, for the finished-goods warehouse. The Municipality verifies zoning compatibility, assesses the municipal fee, and issues the operating notice. This notice is the only physical premises authorization required for the non-industrial business.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate issued by the DGI
Registered Foundation Charter and Public Registry certificate
Copy of lease or ownership title for the commercial premises
Municipal zoning and use certificate (certificado de uso de suelo)
Identity documents of the applicant and resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality rejects the notice because the premises use is inconsistent, either relocate to a commercially zoned property or submit an administrative appeal to the Alcaldía within fifteen business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational and fire safety clearance of the physical premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá and Dirección General de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Arrange an inspection of the office or warehouse to obtain the fire-safety certificate and, where employees will be hired, the occupational health clearance. The inspection verifies emergency exits, fire extinguishers, electrical panel conditions, storage of portable batteries and solar panels, and general workplace safety.
required_dossiers: Aviso de Operación issued by the Municipality
Building plan or layout of the premises
RUC certificate
Details of battery and solar panel storage areas
Fire-safety inspection request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any inspection findings or corrective notices are issued, implement mitigation measures and request a re-inspection within the period ordered; if the certification is withheld, appeal to the Fire Department's technical board and provide proof of correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - the registered business is direct online retail (ISIC 4791) without manufacturing or industrial transformation. If future battery assembly or solar panel manufacturing is added, the Dirección General de Normas y Tecnología Industrial (DGNTI) of the Ministry of Commerce and Industries would become the competent industrial authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial license applies. The only operating authorization is the Aviso de Operación de Establecimiento Comercial issued by the Municipality of Panama after DGI tax registration; no factory or production permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (Ministerio de Ambiente, MiAMBIENTE) - National Environmental Assessment Directorate
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full EIA report; the activity qualifies as Category III registration (or lower) because it is limited to an office and finished-goods warehouse with no industrial processes, no toxic effluent, and no on-site assembly.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge or VOC emission thresholds govern the base operation. The storage area must prevent battery leakage and comply with MiAMBIENTE waste-management rules by segregating damaged batteries as hazardous waste under Law 7 of 2018; all wastewater must remain sanitary and be discharged only to the municipal sewer network.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá for the office and storage areas; structural load and electrical safety review by the Municipal Engineering Directorate; and, for any employees, occupational workplace clearance from the General Directorate of Occupational Risk Prevention of MITRADEL.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Republic of Panama; official portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa; electronic services (Sede Electrónica): https://sede.dgi.gob.pa. Customs and export procedures: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), https://www.ana.gob.pa. Digital certificates for e-invoicing: Autoridad Nacional de Certificación Electrónica (ANCE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: STEP 1: Execute the PIF foundation deed before a Panamanian notary and register it in the Public Registry; the PIF must be permanently represented by a licensed resident agent. STEP 2: The resident agent files the DGI registration application (Formulario de Inscripción) with the certified foundation deed, bylaws (Reglamento), resident agent acceptance, and identification of founder, foundation council (Consejo de la Fundación), and protector (where appointed) to obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente). STEP 3: Where online retail activity is intended, the PIF simultaneously activates the ITBMS taxpayer account and elects its monthly filing calendar. STEP 4: Obtain the Firma Digital from ANCE and activate the Sede Electrónica profile for electronic invoicing. STEP 5: DGI issues the taxpayer registration certificate (carnet de contribuyente) classifying the PIF as a juridical person. Per the internal classification, the PIF carries a minimum capital requirement (foundation endowment, conventionally B/.10,000) evidenced in the deed; no minimum capital deposit is required with the DGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope: The PIF is a distinct juridical person under Law 25 of 1995; Panamanian tax liability attaches only to Panamanian-source income and territorial activities. A purely foreign-asset, passive PIF remains outside the Panamanian tax net; an active e-commerce PIF making local deliveries to Panamanian consumers is subject to territorial ISR on locally sourced profits and must register, collect, and remit ITBMS on taxable domestic supplies. Foreign-source income is not subject to Panamanian income tax, and the PIF is not treated as a pass-through entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not operate US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch elections. Applicable statutory elections: (i) Foundation charter election: the deed may elect a purely patrimonial/passive scope (outside Panamanian commercial taxation) or an active commercial scope (full ISR/ITBMS exposure); the elected scope is binding and must be registered. (ii) ITBMS input-credit election: exporters may elect to offset input ITBMS against output ITBMS or apply for quarterly refunds of excess credits under the Código Fiscal ITBMS rules. (iii) Electronic invoicing mode election: free DGI Sede Electrónica web platform, certified billing software, or an authorized electronic invoicing service provider (PSF). (iv) Simplified small-taxpayer regime election for low-turnover businesses, where applicable under DGI regulations. (v) Territorial taxation is mandatory since the Law 35 de 2019 reform; no worldwide-basis election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios) - Panamanian value added tax, Código Fiscal Arts. 1057 et seq., as regulated by DGI resolutions and Law 66 de 2020.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PAB 0 (USD equivalent) - no economic turnover threshold: every person habitually or occasionally making taxable transfers of goods in Panama, including remote e-commerce sales delivered to Panamanian customers, must register for ITBMS before commencing operations. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies to annual gross turnover of approximately PAB 38,000 per DGI regulations; this affects payment method and filing frequency but does not defer the registration duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing applies to all taxpayers. Invoices are issued exclusively through the DGI Sede Electrónica platform, DGI-certified billing software, or an authorized electronic invoicing service provider connected by API. Each invoice receives DGI digital authorization and bears a machine-readable verification code; large taxpayers transmit transaction-by-transaction in real time, while other taxpayers transmit in batch per DGI schedule. The system comprises sale invoices, export invoices, purchase invoices, and credit/debit notes, with SAF-T-compatible structured data files. E-commerce orders require the issuance of the electronic sale invoice at delivery or shipment, and exports must be invoiced as 'export' type linked to the customs export declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) definitive physical export of goods from Panamanian customs territory, evidenced by an export declaration accepted by ANA; (ii) services provided to non-resident beneficiaries where the economic use occurs abroad and the Panamanian supplier derives export revenue; and (iii) goods delivered from bonded or free-zone premises to foreign destinations under the applicable free-zone regime. For this PIF, cross-border B2C sales of portable solar power equipment qualify for the 0% rate when goods are shipped from Panama to a foreign address with complete export documentation. Local delivery to Panamanian consumers is subject to 7% ITBMS; if fulfillment occurs from a foreign warehouse directly to the buyer, the sale is outside the Panamanian territorial scope and excluded from ITBMS. Input ITBMS attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable and refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / DUA) accepted by ANA with definitive export regime code
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical exit from Panamanian territory
Export-type electronic invoice (Factura Electrónica de Exportación) authorized by the DGI
Inward Remittance Certificate / banking settlement evidence showing receipt of export proceeds
Packing list and certificate of origin (where required)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI scrutinizes export zero-rating claims against customs exit records, e-invoices, and banking settlement evidence. Where zero-rating is improperly claimed or the goods are diverted to the domestic market, the taxpayer must pay the omitted ITBMS at 7% plus monthly surcharges, interest at the official technical rate, and administrative fines of 50% to 200% of the tax omitted under the Código Fiscal. Wilful fraud or falsified export documentation constitutes criminal tax fraud under Ley 70 de 2019, punishable by imprisonment of 3 to 6 years, increased to 10 years in aggravated cases, together with monetary penalties and loss of export incentive benefits. Export records must be retained for a minimum of 5 years, and clawback assessments may be issued retrospectively in accordance with the statute of limitations period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no stand-alone central bank. The Superintendency of Banks of Panama (Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá, SBP) is the primary regulator and supervisor of licensed banks; Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) acts as the fiscal agent of the Republic and manages state accounts; the Financial Analysis Unit (Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF) functions as the national AML/CFT intelligence unit. No institution issues domestic fiat currency or administers exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is fully dollarized: the US Dollar is lawful legal tender under the Currency Law of 1904, and the Panamanian Balboa exists solely as subsidiary coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity. Both current and capital account transactions are fully convertible with no central bank authorization, no exchange licensing, and no repatriation permits. Profit and benefit remittances from a Private Interest Foundation (PIF) are unrestricted at the FX level; however, remittances of Panamanian-source income may attract the territorial income tax and, when applicable, the 10% statutory dividend or benefit distribution withholding tax. For the ISIC 4791 e-commerce export model, income considered sourced outside Panama (offshore retail sales) is outside the Panamanian tax net, and documented foreign sourcing is the treasury cornerstone.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained indefinitely in USD or any freely convertible currency. Administrative obligations are limited to foreign-trade declarations that may be filed through the Single Window for Foreign Trade (SIGA/VUPA) and, where applicable, registration of the exporting entity with the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI); these obligations do not involve FX conversion or central bank reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-to-MEDIUM. Regulated offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) generally do not accept Panamanian PIFs as primary account holders, and no such entity holds a Panamanian banking license, so any deposit-taking or local clearing activity in Panama would contravene Decreto Ley 2 de 2008. Stripe also does not currently onboard Panama-domiciled businesses directly. Recommended blueprint: maintain the Panamanian PIF as the export treasury and contracting vehicle, while establishing a supported payment-acquisition entity in a Stripe-supported market (US/EU) acting as the PSP settlement conduit; the Panamanian accounts then function as the concentrator of USD settlement funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, physical presence of the founding council member or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is MANDATORY for first-time onboarding at the vast majority of SBP-licensed banks, conducted via a face-to-face client interview at the branch together with the PIF's Resident Agent (an SBP-sanctioned attorney). Remote opening by email or video alone is not accepted under SBP Accord 3-2011 unless a full notarized power of attorney (apostilled) is lodged, coupled with a mandatory video-conference interview and the Resident Agent's co-signature on the compliance acceptance form. Power-of-attorney remote opening is viable only with banks that maintain a documented third-party enhanced due diligence process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundational opacity - the absence of a visible trading history and unclear ultimate beneficial ownership structure of the PIF
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the protocolled Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva) filed at the Public Registry; complete UBO register and sworn declaration under Law 23 of 2015; written statement of purpose describing the e-commerce solar portable power retail model; legal opinion from the Resident Agent confirming the PIF's legal existence and control structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Protector/third-party powers creating ambiguity over disposition authority over bank balances
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Regulations (Reglamento) and any Protector appointment instrument, each notarized and apostilled; resolution of the Foundation Council authorizing the specific account opening; list of named signatories with passport copies; committee mandate letter limiting unilateral dispositions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk country nexus of founders or counterparties (e.g., sanctions-listed jurisdictions or offshore tax haven links)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth report with bank statements and evidence of lawful accumulation; sanctions screening (OFAC/EU/UN) results for all founders, signatories and material counterparties; explanation of commercial rationale for any high-risk jurisdiction; independent credit and background report where requested.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance deficiency - the banks may question whether the Foundation conducts genuine business activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed contracts with suppliers and logistics providers; marketplace seller agreements (e.g., Amazon, eBay, own web-store); purchase orders and shipping documents for portable power goods; customer invoices and PSP settlement statements; lease or shared-office arrangement for the Foundation's Panama representative office; corporate expense records demonstrating operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of initial endowment while the Foundation has no contemporaneous operational track record
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Founder's sworn affidavit of lawful funds; notarized source-of-wealth documentation (asset sale, salary, dividend, inheritance) with controlling references; chain of banking records showing the origin of the initial contribution; authorization by the Foundation Council recording the clean source of the endowment capital.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Since Panama is dollarized, a founder capital injection requires no FX conversion and is executed as a straight USD SWIFT MT103 wire to the PIF's operational account in Panama. The remittance should cite in Tag 72 'Foundation endowment contribution under Article 22, Law 25 of 1995' and reference the Foundation charter folio (Ficha), the date of registration, and the Resident Agent's licensing details. The PIF should attach to the transaction record: (a) certified copy of the Foundation Charter; (b) UBO disclosure under Law 23 of 2015; (c) founder's source-of-funds statement; and (d) a Foundation Council resolution approving the lodgment. Panama imposes no mandatory purpose codes; however, to optimize bank auto-filtering the PIF should adopt ISO-20022 / BOE-GPC conventions such as '4700 – Capital Contribution/Foundation Endowment' or '4100 – Related Party Investment'.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed in USD through Panama banks' correspondent clearing network in New York (CHIPS/Fedwire). Primary rails: (i) direct supplier disbursements via SWIFT MT103, referencing in Tags 70/72 the commercial invoice, packing list, and pro-forma invoice numbers; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) under UCP 600 for high-value import commitments, typically at sight with presentation of full set of Bills of Lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of quality and fumigation certificate where goods are physically traded; (iii) documentary collections under URC 522 for bank-mediated document transfer without taking settlement risk; and (iv) payment-acquiring settlement inflows from Stripe or other PSPs routed to the Foundation's Panamanian treasury account by regular USD wires, where the PSP's settlement bank executes the transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (USD/EUR and USD/GBP) with tenors up to 12 months, used solely to hedge retailsale receivables in foreign currencies

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exposure in closed or lightly traded currencies of target retail markets (e.g., CNY), executed by the Panamanian licensed bank's international treasury desk without onshore convertibility requirements
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) converting floating EUR or GBP receipts into fixed USD cash flows
Plain-vanilla FX options (long-only purchased options) to cap adverse currency movements while retaining upside, without creating speculative obligations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee for Private Interest Foundation – Tasa Única Anual (Law 25 of 1995)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance; remitted through the licensed Resident Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 January; first-year fee is prorated by the Resident Agent and payable within 30 days of foundation inscription
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment accrues a 10% surcharge plus default interest under the Panamanian Tax Code; continued non-payment causes loss of good-standing status, Resident Agent resignation, and administrative strike-off of the foundation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Declaration – Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final (Law 129 of 2020)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección Nacional de Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (DNRBF), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 30 days after the foundation's anniversary in the Beneficial Owners Registry; any transfer of beneficial interest must be updated within 15 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to USD 5,000 per violation; the Resident Agent's access may be suspended until cured, blocking issuance of good-standing and legalisation certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Economic Substance Return – Declaración Anual de Sustancia Económica (Law 70 of 2019)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days after the fiscal year-end (by 31 March for 31 December year-ends), per DGI executive decree
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties for non-filing or inaccurate declarations under Law 70 of 2019; the entity may lose its territorial-source tax certificate and become subject to higher AML and tax risk classification.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return – Declaración Anual de Renta (nil declaration where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 15 March following the 31 December fiscal year-end; a nil return is filed when all income derives from foreign sources under territorial taxation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of at least USD 50 plus monthly interest on any tax due; recurring default may trigger suspension of tax registration and coercive collection proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit applies to a Private Interest Foundation without commercial activity in Panama; an independent certified audit is strongly recommended, and normally required by acquiring banks or payment processors (e.g., Stripe/Affirm risk review), where gross annual volume exceeds USD 1,000,000 or when the Foundation Charter mandates audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or Panama GAAP (Normas Contables Aceptadas – NCA) as elected by the Foundation Council; accounting records must evidence the territorial-source income split for cross-border e-commerce sales.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Resident Agent must verify and confirm the foundation's beneficial owners every calendar year; the annual declaration must restate the identity, nationality, and economic interest percentage of each founder, Foundation Council member, and protector holding substantive disposition rights; any transfer of an economic interest must be minuted by the Foundation Council and reflected in the UBO registry within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Protector and Rights-Holders (if appointed)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 to USD 6,000 per annual engagement
